questions.answer: The ammeter measures the current flowing around the loop; disconnecting a wire breaks the loop, so the current stops everywhere and the bulb goes out.
questions.explanation: Scene s1: a circuit is one unbroken loop - break it anywhere and the flow stops everywhere.
questions.prompt: A battery, a bulb and an ammeter are joined by wires into one unbroken loop and the bulb lights. What does the ammeter measure, and what happens to every part of the circuit if one wire is disconnected?

choices.text: Correct - the bulb glows, so it must consume the current
Wrong - the second ammeter reads more, because the bulb adds current
Wrong - the second ammeter also reads 0.5 A, because current is not used up in a series loop
Wrong - the second ammeter reads zero, because all the current stops at the bulb

questions.explanation: The trap is: The bulb uses up the current. The bulb glows and gets hot, so it looks like it consumes the electricity flowing through it. Current is not used up: an ammeter reads the same 0.5 amps on both sides of the bulb.
questions.misconception: The bulb uses up the current.
questions.prompt: In a series circuit an ammeter before a bulb reads 0.5 A. A classmate says the ammeter after the bulb must read less, because the bulb has used some current up. Which statement is correct?

questions.explanation: Scene s4: Ohm's law V = I R rearranged gives I = V / R = 12 / 4 = 3 amps.
questions.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a resistor of 4 ohms. Calculate the current, showing the Ohm's law step.

choices.text: It goes out too, because the circuit is broken
It stays lit, because it sits on its own branch with a complete path
It stays lit only if the broken bulb is replaced first

questions.explanation: Scene s3: in parallel each bulb sits on its own branch - one can fail and the other stays lit.
questions.prompt: Two bulbs are connected in parallel and one bulb breaks. What happens to the other bulb?

questions.answer: 1.5 A, from I = V / R = 6 / 4 = 1.5; halving the voltage halves the current when the resistance is fixed.
questions.explanation: Scene s4: with resistance fixed at 4 ohms the ammeter falls from 3 A to 1.5 A as the battery steps from 12 V to 6 V.
questions.prompt: The battery in question 3 is replaced by a 6 V battery, with the same 4 ohm resistor. Calculate the new current and state the pattern.
